reels.caption:
I used Claude Code to analyze my entire genome to finally find out whether or not I have a genetic condition my Dad has called haemochromatosis…

+ find out a ton more about my body and health as well!
reels.hook_line: This might be the coolest thing that I've done with ClaudeCode out of anything that I've done, and I've built some pretty crazy stuff in my business, but this one has let me know whether or not I have a recessive disease that my dad has that means that he has too much iron in his blood and has to get all his blood taken out.
segs: This might be the coolest thing that I've done with ClaudeCode out of anything that I've done, and I've built some pretty crazy stuff in my business, but this one has let me know whether or not I have a recessive disease that my dad has that means that he has too much iron in his blood and has to get all his blood taken out.

So if you guys have done your ancestry tests or other ones, you know that you kind of get your regions and stuff, but backing this up is obviously your entire genome, and they've got all of your bases logged somewhere.

So you're able to actually download and export this data, and on ClaudeCode, I built a script that analyzes my entire genome, and it's able to, like, finally, I can know whether or not I have this recessive trait.
So it's called hemochromatosis, and it's on my dad's side.
My dad actually has it, that it's a recessive trait, so it can kind of, like, skip a generation.
I can be a carrier, and I may not fully express it.

But basically, what it means is, when he eats a regular diet, like a modern Western diet, he extracts too much iron from the diet because it was an adaptation for when my family, way back in the day when we were living in, well, my ancestors, living in Scotland and also a lot of, like, Viking ancestry as well, back then, the diet was much more basic.
It was like grains and didn't have as much iron in it.
So it was actually an advantage for my ancestors and my dad's ancestors to have this trait where you could have a very high iron level in your blood and stay healthy while eating a shitty diet.
But now that your boy's on the grass-fed steaks and whatnot, it's not a very good thing to have in the modern day or the modern diet.

And so I've been concerned that I've had this, and it kind of gets expressed later in life, but by taking my data from Ancestry, putting it into ClaudeCode, I've been able to literally find out in a few minutes that I don't have it.
I don't have the trait, and that's so good because I can't do needles and I'm really bad with getting blood taken out.
And the only way to treat this disease that my dad has with this condition is to literally go and get, like, a pint of blood taken out every few months.
So I couldn't think of, this has always been, like, a subtle anxiety for me when I thought about it, but as we can see here, we have done the whole analysis, and I have good news.
That means that I'm not going to have hemochromatosis.
Also, it's told me, you guys might know the Gary Brekker stuff about, like, methylation pathways.
This is a whole sort of video on its own, but basically I have 35% reduced enzyme activity, so I may need to take some things here.
Also, it's told me about my dopamine breakdown.
High stress tolerance, perform well under pressure, but maybe need more stimulation to feel motivated.
A bunch of other insights, and this is just, like, scratching the surface.

But yeah, I just wanted to share that because that was probably one of the coolest things that I've been able to do, and I've done a lot with this stuff, but this was a concern for me for a while, and now I get to have a full, like, all of my healthcare data I can pass into this thing and build my own, like, health operating system.
It's just such a good sign for where, like, healthcare is going in the AI age.
So yeah, I thought I'd share that with you guys, but if you guys want to know how I did this, it's pretty straightforward, but I can just reply in the comments or something.

reels.caption: Do I miss New Zealand?
reels.hook_line: Do I miss New Zealand and the simple life?
segs: Do I miss New Zealand and the simple life?

Interestingly, recently I have, and I've, like, lived all over the world since I've left high school, and I haven't really ever missed home, apart from maybe when I went back to New Zealand, I was like, oh, wow, I forgot how awesome this place is, and then it would usually fade by the time it started getting cold again.
But recently I have, and I think it's just, it's been a pretty hectic year for me and the team, a lot of change, and a lot of figuring stuff out.
And so with that, I guess chaos or change, the need for some sort of stability or familiarity has definitely, like, increased on my side.
So I've been missing New Zealand a lot, missing family, missing home, and just the simple life, for sure.

But at the end of the day, comfort is the enemy of growth, and I've looked at my career and what I want to do with my life, and I've gone, look, I don't think I can get that in New Zealand, or I think it's going to be harder to do so than being here in the States.
So I'm in the process of getting my visa to, I actually just submitted it today after basically like three months of part-time work on that thing.
But it's a lot of work, but at the end of the day, that's the price I'm willing to pay for the growth that I want to have in my career and the impact I want to have on my career as well.
So absolutely, I do miss New Zealand, love New Zealand, and I will absolutely be back, but for the next five years or so, I'll be based here in the US.
